chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: There is no problem with the women proceeding (from Muzdalifah) when the night declines, so they pause at the Sacred Monument for an hour, then they are taken to Mina so they pelt the Jamarah, then they wait for an hour, then they shorten (their hair/nails) and go to Mecca so they perform Tawaf, except if they intend that an animal be slaughtered on their behalf, for they appoint someone to slaughter on their behalf.

key_terms.الْجَمْرَةَ: The Jamarah (pillars representing Satan, pelted during Hajj)
key_terms.يَطُفْنَ: They perform Tawaf (circumambulation of the Kaaba)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرْنَ: They shorten (hair/nails, signifying partial release from Ihram)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct ritual procedure for women during the days of Tashreeq in Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical flexibility granted to women in Shia jurisprudence, allowing them to depart Muzdalifah immediately after nightfall rather than waiting for dawn, thereby avoiding the congestion faced by the general populace. It further clarifies the ritual sequence of stoning the Jamarah and performing Tawaf, while noting the specific provision for women to appoint proxies for the sacrificial animal (Hady), reflecting the ease (rukhas) accommodated for their physical circumstances during the pilgrimage.
